passages.text: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Write in a book all the words that I have spoken to you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD gave a message to Jeremiah.
The LORD said, “Write all the words I have spoken to you.
Write them in a book.”
passages.original: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּתָב־ לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל־ סֵֽפֶר׃

passages.text: For behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore from captivity My people Israel and Judah, declares the LORD. I will restore them to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said these words about Israel and Judah.
The LORD said, “Days are coming.
I will bring back My people Israel and Judah from captivity.
I will return them to the land I gave to their fathers.
They will possess that land.”
passages.original: כִּ֠י הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְ֠שַׁבְתִּי אֶת־ שְׁב֨וּת עַמִּ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוּדָ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֗ים אֶל־ הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם וִֽירֵשֽׁוּהָ׃פ

passages.text: These are the words that the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah.
passages.sermon: The LORD is the God of Israel and Judah.\r\nThe LORD spoke words about Israel and Judah.\r\nThese are the words that the LORD spoke.
passages.original: וְאֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶל־ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Yes, this is what the LORD says: “A cry of panic is heard— a cry of terror, not of peace.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says these words.
We hear a cry of panic.
We hear a cry of terror.
We do not hear peace.
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חֲרָדָ֖ה שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ פַּ֖חַד וְאֵ֥ין שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Ask now, and see: Can a male give birth? Why then do I see every man with his hands on his stomach like a woman in labor and every face turned pale?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke these words about Israel and Judah.
He said, “Ask now and see.
Can a man give birth to a child?
Why do I see every man holding his stomach?
They hold themselves like a woman who is giving birth.
Every face has turned pale.”
passages.original: שַׁאֲלוּ־ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ אִם־ יֹלֵ֖ד זָכָ֑ר מַדּוּעַ֩ רָאִ֨יתִי כָל־ גֶּ֜בֶר יָדָ֤יו עַל־ חֲלָצָיו֙ כַּיּ֣וֹלֵדָ֔ה וְנֶהֶפְכ֥וּ כָל־ פָּנִ֖ים לְיֵרָקֽוֹן׃

passages.text: How awful that day will be! None will be like it! It is the time of Jacob’s distress, but he will be saved out of it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking about a future day.
This day will be very great.
No other day will be like it.
This day will bring trouble for Jacob.
Jacob means the people of Israel.
This will be a time of distress for them.
But Jacob will be saved from this trouble.
passages.original: ה֗וֹי כִּ֥י גָד֛וֹל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מֵאַ֣יִן כָּמֹ֑הוּ וְעֵֽת־ צָרָ֥ה הִיא֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִמֶּ֖נָּה יִוָּשֵֽׁעַ׃

passages.text: On that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, I will break the yoke off their necks and tear off their bonds, and no longer will strangers enslave them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He promises a future day.
On that day, the LORD will act.
The LORD will break the yoke from your neck.
He will tear off your bonds.
Strangers will not enslave you anymore.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם׀ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק וְלֹא־ יַעַבְדוּ־ ב֥וֹ ע֖וֹד זָרִֽים׃

passages.text: Instead, they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.
passages.sermon:
The people will serve the LORD.
The LORD is their God.
The people will also serve David.
David will be their king.
The LORD will raise up David for them.
passages.original: וְעָ֣בְד֔וּ אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֵת֙ דָּוִ֣ד מַלְכָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָקִ֖ים לָהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: As for you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. For I will surely save you out of a distant place, your descendants from the land of their captivity! Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Jacob, His servant, and to Israel.
The LORD says, “Do not be afraid, Jacob.
Do not be dismayed, Israel.
I am the LORD.
I will save you from a distant place.
I will save your descendants from the land where they are captives.
Jacob will return home.
Jacob will live in quietness.
Jacob will live in safety.
No one will make Jacob afraid.”
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל־ תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָה֙ וְאַל־ תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת־ זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃

passages.text: For I am with you to save you, declares the LORD. Though I will completely destroy all the nations to which I have scattered you, I will not completely destroy you. Yet I will discipline you justly, and will by no means leave you unpunished.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Jacob, His servant, and to Israel.
The LORD says, "I am with you."
I am here to save you.
I will destroy all the nations where I have scattered you.
I will not destroy you completely.
I will discipline you with justice.
I will not leave you unpunished.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֖ה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל־ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם׀ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִצוֹתִ֣יךָ שָּׁ֗ם אַ֤ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹֽא־ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֙יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ׃פ

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: “Your injury is incurable; your wound is grievous.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is just and holy.
The LORD says this to Israel.
Your injury cannot be healed.
Your wound is very serious.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: There is no one to plead your cause, no remedy for your sores, no recovery for you.
passages.sermon:
No one stands to defend you.
No one argues your case.
You have no remedy for your wounds.
You have no healing for your sores.
You have no cure.
passages.original: אֵֽין־ דָּ֥ן דִּינֵ֖ךְ לְמָז֑וֹר רְפֻא֥וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: All your lovers have forgotten you; they no longer seek you, for I have struck you as an enemy would, with the discipline of someone cruel, because of your great iniquity and your numerous sins.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God says, “All your lovers have forgotten you.
They do not seek you.
I have struck you as an enemy strikes.
I have disciplined you with cruelty.
I did this because your iniquity is great.
You have many sins.”
passages.original: כָּל־ מְאַהֲבַ֣יִךְ שְׁכֵח֔וּךְ אוֹתָ֖ךְ לֹ֣א יִדְרֹ֑שׁוּ כִּי֩ מַכַּ֨ת אוֹיֵ֤ב הִכִּיתִיךְ֙ מוּסַ֣ר אַכְזָרִ֔י עַ֚ל רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ עָצְמ֖וּ חַטֹּאתָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Why do you cry out over your wound? Your pain has no cure! Because of your great iniquity and your numerous sins I have done these things to you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God sees their suffering.
God asks, “Why do you cry out over your wound?”
Your pain is severe.
No one can heal your pain.
You have many sins.
You have done much wrong.
Because of your great iniquity, I have done these things to you.
passages.original: מַה־ תִּזְעַק֙ עַל־ שִׁבְרֵ֔ךְ אָנ֖וּשׁ מַכְאֹבֵ֑ךְ עַ֣ל׀ רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנֵ֗ךְ עָֽצְמוּ֙ חַטֹּאתַ֔יִךְ עָשִׂ֥יתִי אֵ֖לֶּה לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, all who devour you will be devoured, and all your adversaries—every one of them— will go off into exile. Those who plundered you will be plundered, and all who raided you will be raided.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people, Israel.
God promises justice for Israel.
Everyone who devours you will be devoured.
All your enemies will go into exile.
Those who plunder you will be plundered.
Everyone who raids you will be raided.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כָּל־ אֹכְלַ֙יִךְ֙ יֵאָכֵ֔לוּ וְכָל־ צָרַ֥יִךְ כֻּלָּ֖ם בַּשְּׁבִ֣י יֵלֵ֑כוּ וְהָי֤וּ שֹׁאסַ֙יִךְ֙ לִמְשִׁסָּ֔ה וְכָל־ בֹּזְזַ֖יִךְ אֶתֵּ֥ן לָבַֽז׃

passages.text: But I will restore your health and heal your wounds, declares the LORD, because they call you an outcast, Zion, for whom no one cares.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises to restore your health.
The LORD will heal your wounds.
People call you an outcast.
They say you are Zion.
They say no one cares for you.
passages.original: כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י נִדָּחָה֙ קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֔ךְ צִיּ֣וֹן הִ֔יא דֹּרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “I will restore the fortunes of Jacob’s tents and have compassion on his dwellings. And the city will be rebuilt on her own ruins, and the palace will stand in its rightful place.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises to act.
The LORD will restore the fortunes of Jacob’s tents.
Jacob’s tents mean the homes of the people of Israel.
The LORD will have compassion on Jacob’s dwellings.
The city will be rebuilt on its own ruins.
The palace will stand in its rightful place.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִי־ שָׁב֙ שְׁבוּת֙ אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו אֲרַחֵ֑ם וְנִבְנְתָ֥ה עִיר֙ עַל־ תִּלָּ֔הּ וְאַרְמ֖וֹן עַל־ מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ יֵשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: Thanksgiving will proceed from them, a sound of celebration. I will multiply them, and they will not be decreased; I will honor them, and they will not be belittled.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people, Israel.
God promises to bless them.
Thanksgiving will come from them.
They will give thanks.
A sound of celebration will come from them.
They will rejoice.
God will make them many.
They will not become few.
God will honor them.
They will not be belittled.
passages.original: וְיָצָ֥א מֵהֶ֛ם תּוֹדָ֖ה וְק֣וֹל מְשַׂחֲקִ֑ים וְהִרְבִּתִים֙ וְלֹ֣א יִמְעָ֔טוּ וְהִכְבַּדְתִּ֖ים וְלֹ֥א יִצְעָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Their children will be as in days of old, and their congregation will be established before Me; and I will punish all their oppressors.
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God promises to restore His people.
Their children will be as they were long ago.
Their children will be strong and many.
Their community will stand before God.
God will make their congregation firm and secure.
God will punish all who oppress them.
passages.original: וְהָי֤וּ בָנָיו֙ כְּקֶ֔דֶם וַעֲדָת֖וֹ לְפָנַ֣י תִּכּ֑וֹן וּפָ֣קַדְתִּ֔י עַ֖ל כָּל־ לֹחֲצָֽיו׃

passages.text: Their leader will be one of their own, and their ruler will arise from their midst. And I will bring him near, and he will approach Me, for who would dare on his own to approach Me?” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD will give the people a leader.
This leader will come from among the people.
Their ruler will arise from their own midst.
The LORD will bring this leader near to Himself.
This leader will approach the LORD.
No one can approach the LORD on their own.
Only the LORD allows someone to come near.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה אַדִּיר֜וֹ מִמֶּ֗נּוּ וּמֹֽשְׁלוֹ֙ מִקִּרְבּ֣וֹ יֵצֵ֔א וְהִקְרַבְתִּ֖יו וְנִגַּ֣שׁ אֵלָ֑י כִּי֩ מִ֨י הוּא־ זֶ֜ה עָרַ֧ב אֶת־ לִבּ֛וֹ לָגֶ֥שֶׁת אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “And you will be My people, and I will be your God.”
passages.sermon: God speaks to the people of Israel.\r\nGod says, “You will be My people.”\r\nGod says, “I will be your God.”
passages.original: וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Behold, the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful and just.
The LORD sends a storm.
This storm is full of fury.
The storm is like a whirlwind.
The whirlwind comes down.
It comes upon the heads of the wicked.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה׀ סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה סַ֖עַר מִתְגּוֹרֵ֑ר עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל׃

passages.text: The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart. In the days to come you will understand this.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has fierce anger.
The LORD will not turn back His anger.
He will keep His anger until He finishes what He plans.
He will do everything in His heart.
He will accomplish all His purposes.
In the days to come, you will understand this.
passages.original: לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב חֲרוֹן֙ אַף־ יְהוָ֔ה עַד־ עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד־ הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּתְבּ֥וֹנְנוּ בָֽהּ׃
